## IF A TOOL CALL COMES BACK WRONG - CHANGE THE CALL, NEVER REPEAT IT
A malformed call fails the same way every time. Repeating it verbatim burns the run to zero.
- Call rejected / came back malformed -> your ARGUMENTS were wrong, not your diagnosis. Rewrite the call.
- Missing `old_string` -> you emitted `new_string` alone. `edit_file` REQUIRES filepath + old_string + new_string.
- Unclear error -> stop. Make the SMALLEST possible edit: a one-line old_string you have literally just read.

stop matching. The same applies to any "extend this list/pattern/branch" edit: add beside it.

steps.message: The fix ensures that when an empty renderable is provided to `Live`, it renders as many newlines as the previous height to clear the screen and preserves the previous shape so that subsequent updates can correctly reposition the cursor.

The bug was caused by `LiveRender` updating its `_shape` to `(0, 0)` when rendering an empty renderable, which prevented subsequent updates from correctly repositioning the cursor to overwrite the previous content. I modified `rich/live_render.py` to detect empty renderables and, if a previous shape exists, render a number of newlines equal to the previous height and restore the previous shape. This effectively clears the rendered area and maintains the correct cursor offset for future updates.
